title: Domain dynamics within the PriA DNA helicase regulate DNA replication restart.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the Dryad deposit's full metadata and complete file manifest through the Dryad application programming interface (16 files, 1.59 GB total, CC0 licence): three cryo-electron microscopy density maps (.mrc), one video, a README, and 12 zip archives of raw assay output (gel-shift assays 75 MB + 47 MB, helicase assays 142 MB + 23 MB + 22 MB + 13 MB, mass photometry 1,017 MB, ATP-hydrolysis 4.2 MB + 1.2 MB + 0.9 MB, a protein-carbonyl assay 0.06 MB). Downloaded and unpacked the journal supplement zip (25.8 MB): it holds only figure images, a 36-page supplementary PDF and a movie, no data tables. Scanned the open-access full text for every point-mutation token and every supplementary table caption.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The contents inside each Dryad zip. Every Dryad per-file download returned HTTP 401 through the application programming interface and HTTP 403 / an Anubis proof-of-work bot challenge through the web route, so I could not open a single raw file or the README. What is in them is inferred from file names plus the paper's Materials and Methods.

a1_downloadable.note: Public Dryad deposit, CC0 licence, no login or access application. But all automated downloads were blocked (401 from the application programming interface, 403 plus an anti-bot proof-of-work challenge from the web route), so nothing was opened; a human with a browser could get it.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS. No label column exists anywhere. The quantities of interest (maximum reaction velocity, the DNA concentration giving half-maximal velocity, percent DNA unwound) are GraphPad Prism curve fits reported inside figures; the deposited files are raw gel images, mass-photometry movies and absorbance traces. The label would have to be constructed by re-quantifying gels and re-fitting kinetics.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present in principle: the PriA protein sequence (Escherichia coli, UniProt P17888) plus ~15 named point mutations, and ~17 synthetic DNA fork substrates listed in Supplementary Table S1. Not verified in the deposited files.

a4_units_stated.note: Methods state units clearly throughout (nanomolar DNA, 1 mM ATP, absorbance at 340 nm, kilodaltons for mass photometry). But there is no units column because there is no measurement table.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS badly. This is a single-protein structure-function study. The unit of analysis is the PriA variant: I counted 15 distinct point-mutation tokens in the full text (R427A, R427D, R428A, R428D, H437A, D438A, H455A, H483A, S481A, T482A, C479Y, E492A, E492R, H599A, H600A), tested against ~17 fork substrates with three or more replicates. That is tens of measured conditions, far under the ~400 minimum for classification and the ~1,500 for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.6 GB total Dryad deposit; the tabular-ish ATP-hydrolysis archives are only ~6 MB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to disagree about: the paper reports no row counts and the deposit is organised by assay, not by rows. Dryad manifest (16 files) matches the data availability statement's three Electron Microscopy Data Bank accessions (EMD-76387/76388/76389).

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean and physical — coupled-enzyme ATP hydrolysis assays, radiolabelled helicase assays, gel-shift binding, single-molecule mass photometry, and in vivo Escherichia coli growth phenotypes. No model-derived labels. A8 is the one killer this paper passes comfortably.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the obvious backbone for PriA variant effects, but there is no label set to fit a head to.

integration.join_key: UniProt P17888 (Escherichia coli PriA) would join to AlphaFold DB and the Protein Data Bank entries 6DCR and 8FAK, but a join on a single protein adds rows for one protein only.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: joining one protein's 15 hand-picked mutants to any large resource still leaves 15 examples.

controls.positive_control: Would be available in principle (wild-type PriA must come out as the most active variant, and the ATPase-dead Walker-motif control must come out dead), but there is no model to control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=15.
controls.external_validation: Prior PriA studies from the same Keck laboratory (PNAS 2015/2018, Nature Communications 2023) measured overlapping variants, but these are the same lab and the same assays, so they are not independent.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: with roughly 15 PriA point variants and no tabulated activity values, any model would be fitting noise, and a cross-validated number on fewer than 20 examples carries no information.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and DNA fork shape to predict how fast a mutant PriA helicase unwinds DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: for each mutant version of the Escherichia coli PriA protein, its amino-acid sequence plus a description of the synthetic DNA replication fork it was given. Verified count: about 15 mutants and about 17 fork substrates.
plain_idea.predict: Activity readouts — rate of ATP consumption, fraction of DNA unwound, and whether the partner protein PriB binds. True answers come from coupled-enzyme absorbance assays, radiolabelled gel assays and single-molecule mass photometry, all done in one laboratory.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Bacterial replication restart is a potential antibiotic target, so a model of which PriA changes break restart would interest the Keck and Sandler laboratories. But with roughly 15 mutants there is nothing to learn that the paper's own figures do not already show.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict PriA helicase/ATPase activity from protein sequence (ESM-2 embeddings) plus DNA fork architecture. The dataset is roughly 15 point mutants on roughly 17 fork substrates, measured as gel images and absorbance traces with no tabulated outcome column, so there are neither labels nor rows for any supervised model.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated — the project dies before any compute is needed. Sizes come from the Dryad file manifest, which I read directly.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct PriA variants in the paper. I did this: 15 point mutations in the whole text, against ~17 fork substrates. That alone kills it, and it took one grep.

verdict_reason: Single-protein biophysics: ~15 PriA point mutants, no tabulated activity column, raw gels and movies only.
